597085.old: • Sometimes an aromatic group is found as a substituent bonded to a nonaromatic entity or to another aromatic ring. The group of atoms remaining when a hydrogen atom is removed from an aromatic compound is called an aryl group. Phenyl is the only aryl group you need in this course.

597184.old:
Health Career Connection

  • Nursing – sickle cell disease: one DNA base substitution changes codon GAG (Glu) to GUG (Val) in the mRNA for the β chain of hemoglobin (Section 12.7; Chapter 10).
  • Nursing – mRNA vaccines and HIV drugs: an mRNA vaccine is translated by your ribosomes for a few days and never enters the nucleus; HIV drugs block reverse transcriptase and other viral-only enzymes (Section 12.8).
  • Nursing – genetic testing: PCR and sequencing of blood or saliva identify carriers and predict drug metabolism (Section 12.9).
  • Dental hygiene – HPV and cold sores: HPV-16 (a DNA virus) causes most oropharyngeal cancers, so screen at every recall; HSV-1 reactivates as herpes labialis and elective treatment waits until the lesion heals (Section 12.8). Radiographs follow ALARA because ionizing radiation damages DNA (Section 12.7).

10. Recombinant DNA (overview)

Cut (restriction enzyme, a hydrolase, leaves sticky ends), paste (sticky ends pair; DNA ligase re-forms the phosphodiester bonds) into a plasmid vector, copy (bacteria replicate it), express (bacteria make the human protein: insulin, growth hormone, factor VIII, vaccine proteins). PCR copies a stretch of DNA by heat–cool–extend cycles with a heat-stable polymerase. Details and genetic testing: Section 12.9.
